what_happened: Reading check-module-invariants.sh's --emit-inventory implementation (scan() function, live_walk.py's recursive live_files()) directly revealed that README inventory-block staleness is NOT limited to a fixed 2-file set (root README.md + FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md): ~36 README.md files repo-wide register BEGIN GENERATED: inventory blocks, and a .lean edit propagates staleness up the directory-ancestor chain (and via hand-pinned out-of-tree rows like FormalSystem/README.md's pinned ../FormalSystem.lean row). An ancestor-chain membership heuristic (collect every README registering dir=A for A in the edited file's self/ancestor directories up to repo root) reproduces the exact 3-README set (README.md, FormalSystem/README.md, FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md) that task 750 actually needed, without having to special-case rows=loose vs rows=subdirs/totals semantics.

Task 731's own dispatch description quotes an orchestrator postflight ADVISORY naming only two undeclared-scope files (FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md, README.md) for the second of the two precedent tasks, but git log shows that task's commits also touched FormalSystem/README.md's generated block (a pinned ../FormalSystem.lean row). Unable to confirm within this research pass whether FormalSystem/README.md was already in that task's declared file_scope by some other route (making the ADVISORY's two-file list correct for its own 'outside declared scope' comparison) or whether postflight's advisory is self-report-based and simply missed it. Does not block the recommendation (the ancestor-chain heuristic safely over-includes it either way) but is flagged for the plan phase in case exact ADVISORY-matching becomes a verification criterion.

Plan-time reading of orchestrate-batch-admit.sh and lib/file-scope-overlap.sh surfaced a downstream consequence the research report did not cover: appending shared generated surfaces (typst/generated/status.typ, root README.md) to every .lean-touching task's file_scope makes any two concurrent Lean tasks overlap on those paths, which batch-admit turns into a file_scope_collision DEFER and task-lock.sh turns into a lock contention. The plan accepts this (the collision is genuine -- both tasks really do regenerate status.typ and really do fight the pre-commit gate) and documents it rather than adding an exclusion list to the shared overlap library, but it is a real parallelism cost not named in the dispatch.

Sibling task 754 declares .claude/context/formats/plan-format.md in its file_scope this same cycle. Planning deliberately routed the contract-documentation edit to the harvester's own header comment plus context/reference/state-management-schema.md's file-scope section instead of plan-format.md, so this task's declared scope has zero intersection with 754's. The single-point-fix shape also means none of update-task-status.sh / skill-base.sh / orchestrator-postflight.sh (all three in 754's scope) need to change.

Authored all 11 new regression cases (11-21) for test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh in a single batched edit at Phase 1, rather than incrementally across Phases 1-4 as the plan's per-phase Tasks lists specify. Script functionality (the gate, status.typ append, ancestor-chain README scan, narrow globs) is still implemented and committed incrementally per phase; each phase's own narrow verification is checked via direct harvester invocation against that phase's specific fixtures rather than the full suite file (which only turns fully green once Phase 4's script code lands). The full run-all.sh --only three-suite selection is run once all phases' script code is complete, confirming the batched test file passes in full.

Phase 1's progressive handoff (Stage 4D-iii) was not written before Phase 1's closing commit landed, so it is skipped for Phase 1 per the omission allowance (not the last phase, but the oversight is accepted rather than retroactively fixed with a second commit, which would violate the single-commit-per-phase rule). Phases 2-4 write their progressive handoff before their respective closing commits.
